source_note: Rules paraphrased in our own words from the workbooks; tables and quoted sources transcribed as printed. Where the workbooks err, the error is kept as printed and flagged in a note.

rules.title: Verb (פועל):
rules.text: A word that shows an action or a state — e.g. אָכַל, שָׁמַר (actions); עָמַד, יָשַׁן (states).

rules.title: Shoresh / root (שורש):
rules.text: The three (usually) letters that carry the core meaning of a verb family. All words built from one root share its basic idea.

rules.title: Root letters (אותיות השורש):
rules.text: Named by position — פה"פ (first), עה"פ (second), לה"פ (third).

rules.title: Tense (זמן):
rules.text: Past (עבר), present (הווה), future (עתיד). The imperative (ציווי) gives commands; the infinitive (שם הפועל) is the "to ___" form.

rules.title: Person (גוף):
rules.text: Who does the action — 1st/2nd/3rd person, singular/plural, masculine/feminine. Hebrew verbs change form for each person.

rules.title: Musafiot (מוספיות):
rules.text: Extra letters added before or after the root to build verb forms (prefixes like אית"ן, suffixes like תי/תם).

rules.title: Binyan (בנין):
rules.text: One of seven verb "buildings" — patterns that shape how a root is conjugated. Each binyan has its own vowels and prefixes.

rules.title: Gizrah (גזרה):
rules.text: The "form" of a root — whether its letters are all regular (שלמים) or include weak/guttural letters that change the pattern.

rules.title: Scope of this series:
rules.text: These workbooks use only complete roots (גזרת השלמים). Weak-root changes covered here are gutturals and a few assimilations only.

rules.title: Pa'al is the basic binyan.
rules.text: It has no binyan prefix and no dagesh of its own, so it is called "light" (קל). It describes actions (אָכַל, שָׁמַר) and states (עָמַד, יָשַׁן).

rules.title: Past pattern:
rules.text: פָּעַל — kamatz under R1, patach under R2 (שָׁמַר).

rules.title: Present, pattern 1 (most verbs):
rules.text: פֹּעֵל — holam under R1, tzere under R2 (שׁוֹמֵר). Feminine singular שׁוֹמֶרֶת (segol); an older form שׁוֹמְרָה is no longer used.

rules.title: Present, pattern 2 (stative verbs):
rules.text: פָּעֵל — kamatz under R1, tzere under R2 (גָּדֵל). Used for verbs of state (בָּטֵל, בָּשֵׁל, זָקֵן, יָשֵׁן, כָּבֵד).

rules.title: Present, pattern 3 (passive adjective):
rules.text: פָּעוּל — kamatz under R1, shuruk under R2 (יָכוּל; also שָׁבוּר, כָּתוּב, סָגוּר as adjectives).

rules.title: Future, pattern 1:
rules.text: אֶפְעֹל — e.g. אֶשְׁמֹר (holam under R2).

rules.title: Future, pattern 2:
rules.text: אֶפְעַל — e.g. אֶלְמַד (patach under R2). Which pattern a root takes is a property of that root (אֶפְעַל roots include למד, רכב, לבש, גדל).

rules.title: Imperative:
rules.text: Built from the future by dropping the ת prefix (תִּשְׁמֹר → שְׁמֹר). Two patterns, matching the two future patterns. When two shva na'im would come together, the first becomes hirik (שְׁמֹר but שִׁמְרִי, שִׁמְרוּ).

rules.title: Infinitive:
rules.text: לִפְעֹל (לִשְׁמֹר).

rules.title: III-tav assimilation (past):
rules.text: When R3 is ת, it merges with a ת suffix: כָּרַתְתִּי becomes כָּרַתִּי; שָׁבַתְתָּ becomes שָׁבַתָּ.

rules.title: III-nun assimilation (past):
rules.text: When R3 is נ, it merges with a נ suffix: זָקַנְנוּ becomes זָקַנּוּ. (2mp/2fp keep the full form with a shva under R1: זְקַנְתֶּם.)

rules.title: I-guttural (future + imperative):
rules.text: When R1 is a guttural (א/ה/ח/ע), the shva na under it becomes a chataf. The chataf vowel matches the following vowel: אֶעֱבֹד (chataf segol before segol) vs תַּעֲבֹד (chataf patach before patach). Where two shva na'im would otherwise meet, the chataf becomes a full vowel instead (תַּעַבְדִי, יַעַבְדוּ, עִבְדִי, עִבְדוּ).

rules.title: III-guttural (present + infinitive):
rules.text: When R3 is a guttural, a furtive patach appears at the end of the word (שׁוֹמֵעַ, לִשְׁמֹעַ).

rules.title: Modern forms:
rules.text: 2fp/3fp future and 2fp imperative use the masculine plural forms today (תִּשְׁמְרוּ, יִשְׁמְרוּ, שִׁמְרוּ).

rules.title: Meanings:
rules.text: Passive (נִשְׁמַר — was guarded); reflexive (נִלְחַם — fought, lit. "fought himself"); reciprocal (two people acting on each other); change of state (נִרְדַּם — fell asleep); plain action (נִכְנַס — entered).

rules.title: Past pattern:
rules.text: נִפְעַל — nun with hirik, then the root (נִזְכַּר).

rules.title: Present pattern:
rules.text: נִפְעָל — nun with hirik, kamatz under R2 (נִזְכָּר). Feminine singular נִזְכֶּרֶת (segol); an older form נִזְכָּרָה is no longer common.

rules.title: Future pattern:
rules.text: The nun drops and R1 takes a compensatory dagesh: אִזָּכֵר (from *אִנְזָכֵר).

rules.title: Imperative pattern:
rules.text: הִפָּעֵל — הִזָּכֵר (nun drops, dagesh in R1). An imperative exists only for action verbs, not for passive ones (נִשְׁמַר has הִשָּׁמֵר; נִלְמַד has no imperative).

rules.title: Infinitive:
rules.text: לְהִפָּעֵל (לְהִזָּכֵר — nun drops, dagesh in R1).

rules.title: II-guttural:
rules.text: When R2 is a guttural, the shva na under it becomes a chataf (נִלְחֲמָה).

rules.title: I-guttural:
rules.text: When R1 is a guttural, the nun's hirik becomes segol and R1 takes chataf segol (נֶעֱנַשְׁתִּי). In 3fs/3p the chataf becomes plain segol (נֶעֱנְשָׁה, נֶעֱנְשׁוּ). In future/imperative, the assimilated nun's dagesh is "paid back" by lengthening the vowel instead (אֶחָתֵם for *אֶחְתֵּם, הֵרָדֵם for *הִרְדֵּם) — including for ר.

rules.title: III-guttural:
rules.text: When R3 is a guttural, patach is kept where the regular pattern has tzere/segol (אֶשָּׁבַע, נִשְׁבַּעַת, הִשָּׁבַע).

rules.title: Modern forms:
rules.text: 2fp/3fp future and 2fp imperative use the masculine plural forms today.

rules.title: Pi'el is one of the three "strengthening" (חיזוקיים) binyanim.
rules.text: A strong binyan has a dagesh chazak in R2.

rules.title: Meanings:
rules.text: Intensified action (שָׁבַר → שִׁבֵּר, חָשַׁב → חִשֵּׁב); causing an action (לָמַד "learned" → לִמֵּד "taught"); continuing or repeated action (קִפֵּץ, דִּלֵּג); the opposite of the same root in another binyan (שֵׁרֵשׁ "uproot" vs הִשְׁרִישׁ "take root"; סִקֵּל "clear of stones" vs סָקַל "stone"); plain action like Pa'al (דִּבֵּר, צִלֵּם, בִּקֵּשׁ, שִׁלֵּם).

rules.title: Past pattern:
rules.text: פִּעֵל — hirik under R1, tzere under R2, dagesh chazak in R2 (סִדֵּר).

rules.title: Present pattern:
rules.text: מְפַעֵל — מְ prefix, patach under R1, tzere under R2, dagesh in R2 (מְסַדֵּר). Feminine singular מְסַדֶּרֶת (segol).

rules.title: Future pattern:
rules.text: אֹתִין + פַעֵל (אֲסַדֵּר).

rules.title: Imperative:
rules.text: Drop the future ת prefix (תְּסַדֵּר → סַדֵּר).

rules.title: Infinitive:
rules.text: לְפַעֵל (לְסַדֵּר).

rules.title: II-guttural (א/ר):
rules.text: These letters cannot take a dagesh, so the dagesh is "paid back" by lengthening the vowel: hirik becomes tzere in the past (פֵּרֵק), patach becomes kamatz in present/future/imperative (מְפָרֵק, אֲפָרֵק, פָּרֵק). With ה/ח/ע there is no payback and no change.

rules.title: III-guttural (ח/א):
rules.text: A furtive patach appears at the end of the word (שִׂמֵּחַ), and patach forms also exist as alternatives (שִׂמַּח, אֲשַׂמַּח, שַׂמַּח). Present feminine singular takes patach instead of segol (מְשַׂמַּחַת).

rules.title: Look-alike warning:
rules.text: לִמְדוּ (Pa'al imperative, "learn!") vs לִמְּדוּ (Pi'el past, "they taught") — same letters, different dagesh and vowels.

rules.title: Modern forms:
rules.text: 2fp/3fp future and 2fp imperative use the masculine plural forms today.

rules.title: Pu'al is one of the three "strengthening" binyanim (dagesh chazak in R2). It has ONE meaning: passive — the passive of Pi'el
rules.text: (קִשֵּׁט "decorated" → קֻשַּׁט "was decorated").

rules.title: Modern use:
rules.text: Pu'al present forms are widely used as adjectives (אָדָם מְכֻבָּד, אִשָּׁה מְלֻמֶּדֶת).

rules.title: Past pattern:
rules.text: פֻּעַל — kubutz under R1, patach under R2, dagesh in R2 (צֻלַּם).

rules.title: Present pattern:
rules.text: מְפֻעָל — מְ prefix, kubutz under R1, kamatz under R2, dagesh in R2 (מְצֻלָּם). Feminine singular מְצֻלֶּמֶת (segol).

rules.title: Future pattern:
rules.text: אֹתִין + פֻּעַל (אֲצֻלַּם).

rules.title: Imperative: none.
rules.text: You cannot command someone to be acted upon — the action does not depend on them.
Infinitive: none.

rules.title: R1 vowel:
rules.text: The "o" vowel under R1 can appear as kubutz, shuruk, or kamatz katan (מְצֻלָּם, מְאָדָּם — the א has kamatz katan, pronounced "o").

rules.title: II-guttural (א/ה/ע/ר):
rules.text: These letters cannot take a dagesh, so the kubutz becomes holam chaser in all tenses (גֹּרַשׁ, מְגֹרָשׁ, אֶגֹּרַשׁ). With ח there is no payback and no change.

rules.title: Pausal forms:
rules.text: At the end of a pasuk (sof pasuk) or at an etnachta, the vowel changes: future forms that should have patach under R1 take kamatz instead (תְּחֻלַּק, יְשֻׁלַּם, יְכֻפַּר).

rules.title: Modern forms:
rules.text: 2fp/3fp future use the masculine plural forms today.

rules.title: Meanings:
rules.text: Causing an action (גרימת הפעולה); turning an intransitive Pa'al verb transitive; change of state; turning a noun or adjective into a verb (אֹזֶן → הֶאֱזִין "listened", שָׁמֵן → הִשְׁמִין "fattened", שָׁחֹר → הִשְׁחִיר "blackened"); plain action (הִשְׁלִיךְ, הִקְשִׁיב); Nif'al roots used in Hif'il (נִכְנַס → הִכְנִיס); a verb before an infinitive in place of an adjective (הֵיטִיב לְדַבֵּר, הִרְחִיק לָלֶכֶת).

rules.title: Past pattern:
rules.text: הִפְעִיל — הִ prefix, shva under R1, hirik-yod before R3 (הִשְׁלִים).

rules.title: Present pattern:
rules.text: מַפְעִיל — מַ prefix, shva under R1 (מַשְׁלִים). Feminine singular מַשְׁלִימָה; an older form מַשְׁלֶמֶת is no longer used.

rules.title: Future pattern:
rules.text: אֹתִין + פְעִיל (אַשְׁלִים).

rules.title: Imperative:
rules.text: Drop the future ת prefix and replace it with ה (תַּשְׁלִים → הַשְׁלֵם). Pattern הַפְעֵל (tzere under R2). Note: when R2 is ב/כ/פ, it takes a dagesh after the shva nach.

rules.title: Infinitive:
rules.text: לְהַפְעִיל (לְהַשְׁלִים).

rules.title: I-guttural (א/ח/ע):
rules.text: The shva na under R1 becomes a chataf instead. The hirik of the past becomes tzere (הֶעְסִיק), and the patach of present/future/imperative becomes kamatz (מַעֲסִיק, אַעֲסִיק, הַעֲסֵק). Note: ח sometimes keeps its shva (הֶחְזִיק, הֶחְזִיר).

rules.title: III-guttural (א/ח/ע):
rules.text: A furtive patach appears at the end of the word (הִצְלִיחַ). The tzere before a final guttural becomes patach in 2fp/3fp forms (תַּצְלַחְנָה, הַצְלַחְנָה).

rules.title: Modern forms:
rules.text: 2fp/3fp future and 2fp imperative use the masculine plural forms today.

rules.title: Huf'al is a passive binyan (passive). It has ONE meaning: passive — the passive of Hif'il
rules.text: (הִפְחִיד "frightened" → הָפְחַד "was frightened").

rules.title: Past pattern:
rules.text: הָפְעַל — הָ prefix (kamatz katan, pronounced "o"), shva under R1, patach under R2 (הָכְנַס).

rules.title: Present pattern:
rules.text: מָפְעָל — מָ prefix (kamatz), shva under R1, kamatz under R2 (מָכְנָס). Feminine singular מָכְנֶסֶת (segol) is no longer used today.

rules.title: Future pattern:
rules.text: אֹתִין + פְעַל (אָכְנַס).
Imperative: none. Infinitive: none.

rules.title: R1 vowel:
rules.text: In Biblical Hebrew the prefix vowel is kubutz/shuruk (הֻכְנַס); in modern use it is kamatz katan (הָכְנַס, pronounced "hoch-nas").

rules.title: I-guttural (א/ע):
rules.text: R1 takes chataf-kamatz (הָאֳשַׁם, מָאֳשָׁם, אָאֳשַׁם). With ח the conjugation is regular. (The chataf becomes kamatz where two shva na'im would otherwise meet.)

rules.title: II-guttural (א/ה/ח/ע):
rules.text: A chataf-patach comes in place of the shva, and the "a" sound is heard (הָשְׁאֲרָה, הָשְׁאֲרוּ). With ר there is no change.

rules.title: Modern forms:
rules.text: 2fp/3fp future use the masculine plural forms today.

rules.text: Hitpa'el is one of the three "strengthening" binyanim (dagesh chazak in R2).

rules.title: Meanings:
rules.text: Reflexive — the subject acts on itself (הִתְלַבֵּשׁ "dressed himself"); reciprocal — two people acting on each other (הִתְחַתֵּן); passive (הִתְבַּטֵּל, הִתְקַבֵּל); expressing feelings (הִתְנַצֵּל, הִתְחַשֵּׁב, הִתְאַהֵב); pretending (הִתְנַדֵּב "acted generous", הִתְחַפֵּשׂ); change of state (הִתְיַבֵּשׁ, הִתְגַּבֵּר, הִתְקַדֵּם).

rules.title: Past pattern:
rules.text: הִתְפַּעֵל — הִתְ prefix, patach under R1, tzere under R2, dagesh in R2 (הִתְלַבֵּשׁ).

rules.title: Present pattern:
rules.text: מִתְפַּעֵל — מִתְ prefix (מִתְלַבֵּשׁ). Feminine singular מִתְלַבֶּשֶׁת (segol).

rules.title: Future pattern:
rules.text: אֹתִין + תְפַּעֵל (אֶתְלַבֵּשׁ).

rules.title: Imperative pattern:
rules.text: הִתְפַּעֵל (הִתְלַבֵּשׁ).

rules.title: Infinitive:
rules.text: לְהִתְפַּעֵל (לְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ).

rules.title: Special group 1 — R1 is a sibilant (ס/ש/ש):
rules.text: The ת of Hitpa'el and R1 swap places (metathesis, שיכול עיצורים), because ת + sibilant would sound like a foreign "ch"/"tz" cluster. The ת takes a dagesh lene: *הִתְסַפֵּר → הִסְתַּפֵּר; *הִתְשַׁלֵּב → הִשְׁתַּלֵּב.

rules.title: Special group 2 — R1 is ז:
rules.text: The voiced ז turns the ת into ד (voicing assimilation), then metathesis follows (since "dz" is foreign): *הִתְזַמֵּן → *הִדְזַמֵּן → הִזְדַּמֵּן. The ד takes a dagesh lene.

rules.title: Special group 3 — R1 is צ:
rules.text: The ת becomes ט (easier to say before צ), then metathesis follows: *הִתְצַדֵּק → *הִטְצַדֵּק → הִצְטַדֵּק.

rules.title: Special group 4 — R1 is a dental (ד/ט/ת):
rules.text: The ת of Hitpa'el is swallowed into R1, which takes a compensatory dagesh chazak: *הִתְדַּבֵּק → הִדַּבֵּק; *הִתְטַפֵּל → הִטַּפֵּל; *הִתְתַּמֵּם → הִתַּמֵּם.

rules.title: II-guttural (א/ר):
rules.text: Patach becomes kamatz before R2 as payback for the dagesh (הִתְיָאֵשׁ). With ה/ח/ע there is no dagesh and no payback. When R2 is א/ה/ח/ע, a shva na that comes from a vowel becomes chataf-patach (הִתְיָאֲשָׁה, מִתְיָאֲשִׁים). Note: the workbook contradicts itself on ע — its rule text says no payback, but its full tables for יעצ print kamatz (הִתְיָעֵץ), and its infinitive table prints the same root both ways (לְהִתְיָעֵץ vs לְהִתְיַעֵץ). The tables extracted here follow the full paradigm tables (kamatz); treat the ע forms as uncertain.

rules.title: III-guttural (ח/א):
rules.text: A furtive patach appears at the end of the word (הִתְוַכֵּחַ), and patach forms also exist as alternatives (הִתְוַכַּח, אֶתְוַכַּח). Present feminine singular takes patach instead of segol (מִתְוַכַּחַת).

rules.title: Furtive patach (פתח גנובה):
rules.text: A helper patach that "sneaks in" under a final ה/ח/ע to ease pronunciation. It appears only when the preceding vowel is not "a" (תָּפוּחַ, שָׁבוּעַ, גָּבוֹהַּ).

rules.title: Modern forms:
rules.text: 2fp/3fp future and 2fp imperative use the masculine plural forms today.

past.text: וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלַי ה' אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי לְפָנָיו
וַיֻּגַּד לַאֲבִימֶלֶךְ כִּי הִתְקַבְּצוּ כָּל בַּעֲלֵי מִגְדַּל שְׁכֶם
לֹא הָיָה כְאַחְאָב אֲשֶׁר הִתְמַכֵּר לַעֲשׂוֹת הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי ה'
כֹּה אָמַר ה' אֱלֹקֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר הִתְפַּלַּלְתָּ אֵלַי

present.text: וַתֵּרֶא כִּי מִתְאַמֶּצֶת הִיא לָלֶכֶת אִתָּהּ
וְהִנֵּה צְלִיל לֶחֶם שְׂעֹרִים מִתְהַפֵּךְ בַּמַּחֲנֶה
וְהָיִיתְ כְּאִשָּׁה זֶה יָמִים רַבִּים מִתְאַבֶּלֶת עַל מֵת
וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ אֶת קוֹל ה' אֱלֹקִים מִתְהַלֵּךְ בַּגָּן

future.text: וַיִּתְנַצְּלוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת עֶדְיָם מֵהַר חוֹרֵב

imperative.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ כָל הָעָם אֶל שְׁמוּאֵל הִתְפַּלֵּל בְּעַד עֲבָדֶיךָ

review.text: הִתְפַּלֵּל אֶל ה' וְיָסֵר מֵעָלֵינוּ אֶת הַנָּחָשׁ
וְגַם הַכֹּהֲנִים הַנִּגָּשִׁים אֶל ה' יִתְקַדָּשׁוּ
רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר עֲשֵׂה לְךָ רַב וְהִסְתַּלֵּק מִן הַסָּפֵק
בַּת עַמִּי חִגְרִי שַׂק וְהִתְפַּלְּשִׁי בָאֵפֶר
רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אַל תִּסְתַּכֵּל בַּקַּנְקַן אֶלָּא בְמַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ
תִּשְׁתַּפֵּכְנָה אַבְנֵי קֹדֶשׁ בְּרֹאשׁ כָּל חוּצוֹת
